summary: Stanislav Mudra is an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. from Charles University's Faculty of Arts in Prague, studying under doctoral supervisor Otakar Pertold.

Stanislav Šmelhaus was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Charles University's First Faculty of Medicine (~1906–1912) and earned his Ph.D. from its Faculty of Arts (~1919–1925) under doctoral supervisor Josef Zubatý.

Stanisław Franciszek Michalski was an Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw, earned a Ph.D. at Vienna under Leopold von Schroeder and Paul Kretschmer, and studied at Göttingen under Hermann Oldenberg and Jacob Wackernagel. He lectured at Łódź (1945–1960).

Stanisław Schayer was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied in Warsaw, Heidelberg, Freiburg (Ph.D.), Munich, and Lviv (Habilitation). He held multiple posts at the University of Warsaw, becoming ordinarius Professor in 1938.
Stanley Abe is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. His academic posts include affiliations with Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

Stanley Cecil Sutton worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Librarian at the Commonwealth Relations Office (attested 1953) and at the India Office Records (attested 1974).

Stanley Insler was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at Columbia, Tübingen, and Yale (Ph.D.). He served as Edward E. Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale (~1978–2012).

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Ceylon, Cornell (Ph.D.), and Harvard. He taught at the University of Ceylon, Cambridge, and Chicago, before serving as Professor of Anthropology at Harvard (1976–2001).

Stanley Lombardo is a scholar in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin, and held a post at the University of Kansas (~1976–2014).

Stanley Weinstein was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa, Tokyo, and Harvard (Ph.D.), and taught at Komazawa, SOAS University of London, and Yale University, where he was appointed Emeritus Professor in 1968.

Stanley Wolpert was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. After studying at the City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, he served at the University of California, Los Angeles, becoming department chair in 1967.
Stefan Anacker was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970) under the supervision of Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who completed his dissertation at the University of Washington. His posts include lead researcher roles at the University of Munich and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2012).

Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Leopold von Schroeder, Richard Simon, Sylvain Lévi, and Andrzej Gawroński, among others. He succeeded Gawroński in 1928 and served as a professor at the University of Lviv (1928–1941).

Stefan Larsson is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at Stockholm University. His posts include researcher at Stockholm University (1991–2012) and KTH (2015), and senior lecturer at the University of Gävle (attested 2019).

Stefan Mario Maul is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Freie Universität Berlin, and has served as Ordinarius for Assyriology at Heidelberg University since 1995 and as research director at Heidelberg Academy of Sciences since 2004.

Stefan Mladenov was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Sofia, Vienna, Saint Petersburg, and Charles University (Ph.D.). He spent his career at Sofia University, becoming ordinary Professor of General, Comparative and Indo-European Linguistics in 1921.

Stefania Travagnin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor and centre director at the University of Groningen (~2013–2020) and joined SOAS University of London around 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who earned his degrees at Ca' Foscari University of Venice. He held posts at Ca' Foscari, Soka University's IRIAB, and served as Yehan Numata Professor at Oxford (2012–2020).

Steffen Döll is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Munich and Kyoto University. After serving as an assistant in Munich, he became Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg in 2015.
